summary: Log observation tower on the Blue Ridge Parkway built to look like a tobacco barn; dated 1935 or 1942 by different sources; public picnic-area tower, standing.

facts.design: Log observation tower about 20 feet high, built to look like an old tobacco barn

access.note: Managed as a picnic area beside the Blue Ridge Parkway with parking; the tower is open to climb by a single flight of stairs

visit.trail_note: Park beside the Parkway and walk up the single flight of stairs to the top

events.note: Register 'Built' field; disputed by the 1942 date below
Park Service says the Virginia State Forest Service first erected it; a Commons photo caption gives the same year; disputed by the register's 1935
Registered September 3, 2014; nominated by Kristin Scholetzky

evidence.quote: Built in the 1930's as a fire lookout

evidence.supports: 20 feet high, built to look like an old tobacco barn
evidence.quote: it is a 20 feet high tower, built to look like an old tobacco barn

evidence.supports: administered by the National Park Service
erected by the Virginia State Forest Service in 1942; used to look for hazards or fires
evidence.quote: Originally erected by the Virginia State Forest Service in 1942, it was used to view mountain ranges and look for hazards or fires.

evidence.supports: single flight of stairs to the top; visitors may climb
evidence.quote: If you walk up the single flight of stairs to the top of the tower

evidence.supports: views of Buffalo Mountain and Rich Hill from the top
evidence.quote: views of Buffalo Mountain, Rich Hill, and others
With 28 picnic sites, there's room to spread out at Groundhog Mountain.

evidence.supports: constructed by the Virginia State Forest Service in 1942 (photo caption)
evidence.quote: constructed by the Virginia State Forest service in the summer of 1942

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The firelookout.org list calls the tower two-story; the Park Service mentions a single flight of stairs to the top, and the register gives a 20-foot height. The story uses the height and does not state a story count.

notes_for_editor: Build date is disputed and left open: the register says 1935 (Built field, and 1930s in the description); the Park Service and a Wikimedia Commons caption say the Virginia State Forest Service erected it in 1942. The story gives both. Not checked whether an earlier lookout stood on the site, which could explain the gap. The brief's kind 'two_story' is from the firelookout.org list only. The Forest Lookouts Groundhog page (easternuslookouts.weebly.com) yielded only its heading. The Wikidata entry (Q86868239) showed no inception value in the grep. Leads not read: visitpatrickcounty.org (says the Forest Service used it to watch for fires) and parkwolf/fancygap guide pages. No staffing history was found.
